description: Three-stage check over a parametric trigger. Step 1 aggregates hash-pinned measurement receipts into an index value under a caller-declared metric, aggregation, and window, and stops the chain when there is insufficient evidence. Step 2 evaluates that index value against the caller-supplied threshold, coverage amount, and parametric limit, and returns trigger hit, trigger fraction, and payout amount. Step 3 aggregates the run's execution hashes into a session receipt. art-251 triggers on the high side only: index_value at or above threshold, so low-side perils such as drought cannot be modeled with this chain. Step 2's inputs contain no metric name, and unit equality is never checked, so the caller must use the same unit for the index and the threshold. Headline example: summed rainfall in millimetres over a window, against a threshold in millimetres. The verdict is an arithmetic finding under the policy terms supplied, not a settlement decision, and not actuarial, legal, or regulatory advice.
name: parametric-index-to-trigger-payout-check

steps.handoff: Aggregates hash-pinned receipts into output_payload.index_value under a caller-declared metric, aggregation, and window. When output_payload.insufficient_evidence is true, the chain ends here and the payout run is not started, because a 0 index must never reach the payout. Stage 1 of 3.

Evaluates the cited output_payload.index_value as index_value against the caller-supplied threshold, coverage_amount, and parametric_limit, and returns trigger_hit, trigger_fraction, and payout_amount. art-251 triggers on the high side only: index_value at or above threshold. This run's inputs contain no metric name, and unit equality is never checked, so the caller must use the same unit for the index and the threshold. Stage 2 of 3.
Produces session_receipt_root, the Merkle root over the run's execution_hashes (final stage).

title: Parametric Index to Trigger Payout Check
